Layer 1 Festus Keyamo, Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development
ABUJA—The Federal Government has signed a 30-year concession agreement for the Port Harcourt International Airport, as part of efforts to attract private investment, improve operational efficiency and unlock the economic potential of the nation’s loss-making airports.
Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Mr. Festus Keyamo, disclosed this, yesterday, in Abuja during the signing of the concession agreement with Port Harcourt Airport Company Limited.
Keyamo said the concession was aimed at improving the operational efficiency of the airport, boosting revenue generation and unlocking its commercial potential.
He explained that the Federal Government has been using profits generated from major airports to subsidise the operations of other airports that were running at a loss.
“Some of our airports are being run at a loss. We make so much money from some of our primary airports, and most of those profits are ploughed into running other airports,” Keyamo said.
He noted that the concession had the approval of President Bola Tinubu and the Federal Executive Council, adding that the process was not a sudden decision but one that successive administrations had struggled to implement.
Keyamo said previous attempts to concession airports were frustrated by resistance from labour unions and court cases involving the government.
He, however, attributed the successful conclusion of the process to negotiations with aviation unions, saying the government had secured their agreement before signing the deal.
The minister assured workers that the concession would not lead to job losses or a reduction in their conditions of service.
He said Tinubu had directed that the welfare of aviation workers must be protected throughout the concession process.
“President Bola Tinubu was very concerned about that, that no worker should lose his job. The conditions of service should remain the same,” he said.
Keyamo added that the concessionaire would be subjected to performance reviews every five years to ensure compliance with the terms of the agreement.
He warned that the government could take back the airport if the concessionaire failed to meet the agreed standards.
